title: performance canary: enhanced auto-detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: We need more robust continuous performance canaries that automatically detect latency and throughput regressions, reduce false positives via hysteresis and KV-aware metrics, and enforce safe rollout guards (traffic gating, automatic rollback, and staged traffic shifts). This change adds an enhanced detector, hysteresis thresholds for percentiles and KV-cache hit-sensitive metrics, a pluggable rollout guard that integrates with the routing layer, and observability improvements for investigating regressions. Key behaviors: 1) Detector uses percentile+rate combined signal (p50/p90/p99 + qps derivative) and KV-cache hit rate to reduce noisy alerts for cold-cache spikes. 2) Hysteresis window and sensitivity tuning per-model and per-capacity-pool to avoid flip-flop during transient spikes. 3) Rollout guard implements staged traffic shifting (0->10->50->100) with automated rollback on sustained violations and optional manual override. 4) Integration with perf-canary dashboard and alerting so SREs can see contributor metrics and rollback history. Implementation notes: added new detector algorithm in perf-canary/detector.py, rollout guard in serving/routing/rollout_guard.go, policy config + defaults in perf-canary/configs/defaults.yaml, test coverage in tests/perf/integration_perf_canary.py, and dashboard schema updates under redwood-console/dashboards/perf_canary.json. Backwards compatibility: default heuristics match previous behavior; rollout guard is opt-in via feature flag 'perf_canary_rollout_v2' until fully enabled. Rollout plan: staged beta across a small Dedicated customer pool, then gradual enablement tied to Linear ENG-7234. Related: ENG-7234 (detector tuning), ENG-7240 (rollout policy), docs updated for operators. The description below includes a short checklist for reviewers and a summary of validation steps performed.

review_comments: Lucas Kim (2026-02-19): Nice work, the hysteresis reduces noise in our staging runs. A couple of questions: 1) How does the detector behave with very low QPS models? 2) Can we make the KV weight per-model optional?

Maya Chen (2026-02-19): Reply: For low QPS we increase the aggregation window and lower sensitivity by default; see defaults.yaml. KV weight is optional and defaults to 0.3 but can be 0 for models without cache usage.
Priya Desai (2026-02-20): Please add a note in docs about the experimental feature flag and a migration path for customers on Dedicated.
Maya Chen (2026-02-20): Added feature flag notes in docs and created a Linear task to coordinate beta customers.
Ethan Park (2026-02-22): Left a small nit on naming in rollout_guard.go; otherwise approving. Also ran canary load and observed no false positives over a 48h run.
Maya Chen (2026-02-22): Addressed naming nit and pushed follow-up commit; thanks for verification.

release_notes: Added enhanced performance canary detector (percentile+QPS+KV-weighted), hysteresis tuning, and a pluggable rollout guard with staged traffic shifting and automatic rollback. Opt-in via feature flag perf_canary_rollout_v2. Recommended: monitor perf_canary.detector_score and perf_canary.rollout_actions during initial rollout. See docs/perf-canary.md for tuning guidance.
testing_and_validation: Ran unit tests, integration perf scenarios simulating latency regressions, 48h staging canary with mixed model sizes, and manual rollback tests. Verified stability with low-QPS models and compatibility with existing canary dashboards.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated by perf_canary_rollout_v2. Default heuristics preserve previous thresholds. For Dedicated customers enable in a small pool first; increment stage percentages over 24-72h. If detector_score stays > threshold for hysteresis_duration, automated rollback occurs and a perf_canary.rollout_actions event is emitted.
